meta.title: ANATOMICA shell records — Milestone 16 (Body Model v1, all systems)

records.name: Frontal bone
records.description: Forms the forehead, the roof of the orbits and most of the anterior cranial floor.

records.name: Parietal bone (right)
records.description: Forms the sides and roof of the cranium; the two parietals meet at the sagittal suture.

records.name: Temporal bone (right)
records.description: Houses the external and internal ear and the mastoid process; its mandibular fossa receives the mandibular condyle.

records.name: Parietal bone (left)
records.description: Forms the sides and roof of the cranium; the two parietals meet at the sagittal suture.

records.name: Temporal bone (left)
records.description: Houses the external and internal ear and the mastoid process; its mandibular fossa receives the mandibular condyle.

records.name: Occipital bone
records.description: Forms the posterior cranium; its foramen magnum transmits the spinal cord and it articulates with the atlas.

records.name: Sphenoid bone
records.description: Keystone bone of the cranium, articulating with all other cranial bones; its sella turcica cradles the pituitary gland.

records.name: Ethmoid bone
records.description: Forms the medial orbital walls, the nasal cavity roof and the superior and middle nasal conchae.

records.name: Maxilla (right)
records.description: Upper jaw bone; bears the upper teeth and forms the floor of the orbit and the hard palate with its pair.

records.name: Zygomatic bone (right)
records.description: Cheek bone; its temporal process completes the zygomatic arch with the temporal bone.

records.name: Nasal bone (right)
records.description: Small oblong bone forming the bridge of the nose.

records.name: Lacrimal bone (right)
records.description: Smallest facial bone; forms part of the medial orbital wall and the nasolacrimal canal.

records.name: Palatine bone (right)
records.description: L-shaped bone forming the posterior hard palate and part of the nasal cavity and orbit floors.

records.name: Inferior nasal concha (right)
records.description: Scroll-like bone projecting from the lateral nasal wall, increasing the mucosal surface area.

records.name: Maxilla (left)
records.description: Upper jaw bone; bears the upper teeth and forms the floor of the orbit and the hard palate with its pair.

records.name: Zygomatic bone (left)
records.description: Cheek bone; its temporal process completes the zygomatic arch with the temporal bone.

records.name: Nasal bone (left)
records.description: Small oblong bone forming the bridge of the nose.

records.name: Lacrimal bone (left)
records.description: Smallest facial bone; forms part of the medial orbital wall and the nasolacrimal canal.

records.name: Palatine bone (left)
records.description: L-shaped bone forming the posterior hard palate and part of the nasal cavity and orbit floors.

records.name: Inferior nasal concha (left)
records.description: Scroll-like bone projecting from the lateral nasal wall, increasing the mucosal surface area.

records.name: Vomer
records.description: Thin quadrilateral bone forming the posteroinferior part of the nasal septum.

records.name: Mandible
records.description: The lower jaw and only movable skull bone; bears the lower teeth and articulates at the temporomandibular joints.

records.name: Malleus (right)
records.description: Hammer-shaped ossicle attached to the tympanic membrane, first of the auditory chain.
records.geometry_note: no FMA concept exists in the BodyParts3D 4.0 release for this bone (Milestone 2/3 gap analysis)

records.name: Incus (right)
records.description: Anvil-shaped middle ossicle transmitting vibration from malleus to stapes.
records.geometry_note: no FMA concept exists in the BodyParts3D 4.0 release for this bone (Milestone 2/3 gap analysis)

records.name: Stapes (right)
records.description: Stirrup-shaped ossicle; its footplate fills the oval window of the inner ear.
records.geometry_note: no FMA concept exists in the BodyParts3D 4.0 release for this bone (Milestone 2/3 gap analysis)

records.name: Hyoid bone
records.description: U-shaped bone in the neck that articulates with no other bone; it anchors the tongue and is suspended by muscles and ligaments.

records.name: Atlas (C1)

records.name: Axis (C2)

organ.heart.arterial_supply: Right and left coronary arteries, arising from the right and left aortic sinuses of the ascending aorta; see the coronary records. The sinoatrial nodal artery is a branch of the right coronary artery; the AV node is supplied via a septal perforating branch of the RCA in 90% of people (S6).
organ.heart.chambers: Four chambers: right atrium (receives systemic venous blood), right ventricle (pumps to the pulmonary circuit), left atrium (receives the pulmonary veins), left ventricle (pumps to the systemic circuit; thickest wall).
organ.heart.conduction_system: Sinoatrial (SA) node: pacemaker of the heart, in the right atrium, initiates each beat. Atrioventricular (AV) node: delays the impulse in the interatrial septum region. AV bundle (bundle of His): the only electrical connection between atria and ventricles; divides into right and left bundle branches in the interventricular septum. Purkinje fibres distribute the impulse through the ventricular myocardium.
organ.heart.name: Heart
organ.heart.note: Geometry links the BP3D heart organ record and its part records (chambers, valves, fibrous skeleton). The conduction system, septa, chordae and pericardium are absent from the BP3D release and are flagged, not modelled.
organ.heart.valves: Four valves ensure unidirectional flow: tricuspid (right atrioventricular, three cusps), mitral/bicuspid (left atrioventricular, two cusps), pulmonary semilunar (right ventricle to pulmonary trunk), aortic semilunar (left ventricle to aorta). AV valve cusps are restrained by chordae tendineae attached to papillary muscles.
organ.heart.venous_drainage: Most venous blood of the heart wall drains via the coronary sinus into the right atrium; the right atrium also receives the superior and inferior venae cavae.

artery.arch-of-aorta.territory: Head, neck and upper limbs via its three branches (proximal to distal: brachiocephalic trunk, left common carotid, left subclavian).

artery.descending-thoracic-aorta.course: Descends through the posterior mediastinum, moving from the left of the vertebral column towards the midline, to the aortic hiatus of the diaphragm at T12.
artery.descending-thoracic-aorta.name: Thoracic aorta
artery.descending-thoracic-aorta.origin: Continuation of the aortic arch at the lower border of T4.
artery.descending-thoracic-aorta.termination: Becomes the abdominal aorta at the aortic hiatus (T12).
artery.descending-thoracic-aorta.territory: Bronchial and peribronchial tissue and visceral pleura; posterior mediastinum; oesophagus; dorsal pericardium; superior diaphragm; intercostal spaces 3-11 (nine pairs of posterior intercostal arteries) and the anterolateral abdominal wall (subcostal).
verify: branches: the named branch classes are recorded as unpaired class names; the release lateralises several of them per side - verify

branches: the following names are given by the consulted sources but have no matching concept or record in the BP3D 4.0 release, and are carried as sourced text only: 'mediastinal artery'; 'pericardial artery'; 'superior phrenic artery' - verify

artery.abdominal-aorta.course: Descends anterior to the vertebral column, about 13 cm, to the level of L4.
artery.abdominal-aorta.name: Abdominal aorta
artery.abdominal-aorta.origin: Begins at the aortic hiatus of the diaphragm at T12.
artery.abdominal-aorta.termination: Bifurcates into the right and left common iliac arteries at L4.
artery.abdominal-aorta.territory: Diaphragm; foregut (coeliac); midgut (SMA); adrenal glands; kidneys; gonads; hindgut (IMA); coccyx, lumbar vertebrae and sacrum (median sacral); abdominal wall and spinal cord (four pairs of lumbar arteries); pelvis and lower limbs via the common iliacs.

branches: the following names are given by the consulted sources but have no matching concept or record in the BP3D 4.0 release, and are carried as sourced text only: 'gonadal artery' - verify

artery.brachiocephalic-artery.course: Ascends and divides into the right common carotid and right subclavian arteries.
artery.brachiocephalic-artery.name: Brachiocephalic artery
artery.brachiocephalic-artery.origin: First and largest branch of the aortic arch.
artery.brachiocephalic-artery.termination: Divides into the right common carotid and right subclavian arteries.
artery.brachiocephalic-artery.territory: Right side of the head and neck, and the right upper limb.

artery.common-carotid-artery.course: Ascends through the neck within the carotid sheath, under cover of the anterior border of sternocleidomastoid.
artery.common-carotid-artery.name: Common carotid artery
artery.common-carotid-artery.origin: Right: from the brachiocephalic artery behind the right sternoclavicular joint. Left: directly from the aortic arch in the superior mediastinum.
artery.common-carotid-artery.termination: Divides into the external and internal carotid arteries at the upper border of the thyroid cartilage (level of C4).
artery.common-carotid-artery.territory: The majority of the head and neck.
verify: branches: the following names are given by the consulted sources but have no matching concept or record in the BP3D 4.0 release, and are carried as sourced text only: 'external carotid artery' - verify

artery.external-carotid-artery.course: Ascends superiorly through the neck and terminates within the parotid gland.
artery.external-carotid-artery.name: External carotid artery
artery.external-carotid-artery.note: Major data gap: the external carotid artery itself and most of its named branches are absent from the BP3D 4.0 release; this record is clinical text only in v1. See MILESTONE-5.md.
artery.external-carotid-artery.origin: Terminal branch of the common carotid artery, arising at the level of C4 within the carotid triangle.
artery.external-carotid-artery.termination: Divides into its terminal branches, the maxillary and superficial temporal arteries, within the parotid gland.
artery.external-carotid-artery.territory: The neck, face and scalp (the main arterial supply to these structures).
verify: geometry: the external carotid artery has NO concept of its own in the BP3D 4.0 release (the carotid concepts present are the common carotid artery, the internal carotid artery and their subdivisions), so no inventory record exists to link - verify

branches: 'superior thyroid artery', 'lingual artery' and 'facial artery' are named in S2 but have NO concepts in the BP3D release (stem search over all six release tables returned no matches); the external carotid system in this release is therefore unmodelled - verify

branches: the following names are given by the consulted sources but have no matching concept or record in the BP3D 4.0 release, and are carried as sourced text only: 'ascending pharyngeal artery'; 'occipital artery'; 'posterior auricular artery'; 'maxillary artery'; 'superficial temporal artery' - verify

artery.internal-carotid-artery.course: Ascends through the neck without giving branches, enters the skull via the carotid canal, and passes through the cavernous sinus to the intracranial cavity.
artery.internal-carotid-artery.name: Internal carotid artery
artery.internal-carotid-artery.origin: Terminal branch of the common carotid artery at the level of C4.
artery.internal-carotid-artery.termination: Terminates intracranially as the anterior and middle cerebral arteries.
artery.internal-carotid-artery.territory: The brain (anterior circulation: frontal and parietal lobes, lateral temporal lobes, anterior deep cerebrum), orbit, forehead and nose.
verify: branches: the following names are given by the consulted sources but have no matching concept or record in the BP3D 4.0 release, and are carried as sourced text only: 'middle cerebral artery' - verify

artery.vertebral-artery.course: Ascends through the transverse foramina of the cervical vertebrae (C6-C1), curves around the atlas and enters the cranial cavity via the foramen magnum.
artery.vertebral-artery.name: Vertebral artery
artery.vertebral-artery.origin: Paired branch of the first part of the subclavian artery.
artery.vertebral-artery.termination: The two vertebral arteries unite at the medullopontine junction to form the basilar artery.
artery.vertebral-artery.territory: Posterior circulation of the brain: brainstem, cerebellum, occipital lobes, medial temporal lobes and thalamus; also the spinal cord.

artery.basilar-artery.name: Basilar artery
artery.basilar-artery.origin: Formed by the union of the two vertebral arteries at the medullopontine junction.
artery.basilar-artery.termination: Divides into the two posterior cerebral arteries.
artery.basilar-artery.territory: Brainstem (pontine branches), cerebellum, and the posterior cerebrum via the posterior cerebral arteries.
verify: branches: pontine branches are described in S9 but are not enumerated as named branches here - verify
branches: 'posterior cerebral artery' is named in S9 but has no concept of its own in the BP3D release - verify

artery.anterior-cerebral-artery.course: Courses medially above the optic nerve towards the longitudinal fissure; the two arteries are joined by the anterior communicating artery.
artery.anterior-cerebral-artery.name: Anterior cerebral artery
artery.anterior-cerebral-artery.origin: Terminal branch of the internal carotid artery.
artery.anterior-cerebral-artery.territory: The medial aspects (anteromedial portion) of the cerebral hemispheres.
verify: termination: not sourced from consulted sources - verify

artery.middle-cerebral-artery.course: Runs laterally into the lateral (Sylvian) fissure.
artery.middle-cerebral-artery.name: Middle cerebral artery
artery.middle-cerebral-artery.note: Clinical text only in v1: the vessel itself is absent from the source tables although its branches are present. See MILESTONE-5.md.
artery.middle-cerebral-artery.origin: The lateral continuation of the internal carotid artery at its termination.
artery.middle-cerebral-artery.territory: The lateral aspects of the cerebral hemispheres (the majority of the lateral part of the brain).

artery.posterior-cerebral-artery.course: Courses around the midbrain to the posterior cerebrum; joined to the internal carotid system by the posterior communicating artery.
artery.posterior-cerebral-artery.name: Posterior cerebral artery
artery.posterior-cerebral-artery.note: Clinical text only in v1: the vessel itself is absent from the source tables although a named branch is present. See MILESTONE-5.md.
artery.posterior-cerebral-artery.origin: Terminal branch of the basilar artery.
artery.posterior-cerebral-artery.territory: The medial and lateral parts of the posterior cerebrum (occipital lobes, medial temporal lobes).
verify: geometry: the posterior cerebral artery has NO concept of its own in the BP3D 4.0 release - only its posteromedial central branch exists as a class with lateralised records - so no inventory record exists to link - verify
termination: not sourced from consulted sources - verify

artery.subclavian-artery.course: Courses laterally between the anterior and middle scalene muscles; divided into three parts by the anterior scalene (first: origin to medial border; second: posterior to the muscle; third: lateral border to the lateral border of the first rib).
artery.subclavian-artery.name: Subclavian artery
artery.subclavian-artery.origin: Right: from the brachiocephalic trunk. Left: directly from the aortic arch.
artery.subclavian-artery.termination: Becomes the axillary artery at the lateral border of the first rib.
artery.subclavian-artery.territory: The upper limb, with contributions to the head and neck (circle of Willis via the vertebral artery, thyroid and breast tissue).
verify: branches: 'dorsal scapular artery' is listed in S8 as an additional branch; the BP3D record partition carries it within the subclavian records - verify

artery.internal-thoracic-artery.course: Descends into the thorax behind the costal cartilages, lateral to the sternum.
artery.internal-thoracic-artery.name: Internal thoracic artery
artery.internal-thoracic-artery.note: Surgically load-bearing as the left internal mammary artery graft in coronary bypass; course detail beyond S8 is flagged, not entered.
artery.internal-thoracic-artery.origin: Branch of the first part of the subclavian artery.
artery.internal-thoracic-artery.territory: Anterior thoracic wall and breast tissue.
verify: branches: anterior intercostal, perforating and terminal (musculophrenic, superior epigastric) branches are not enumerated in the consulted sources - verify
termination: not stated in the consulted sources - verify

artery.thyrocervical-trunk.course: Short trunk at the root of the neck, dividing almost immediately.
artery.thyrocervical-trunk.name: Thyrocervical trunk
artery.thyrocervical-trunk.origin: Branch of the first part of the subclavian artery.
artery.thyrocervical-trunk.termination: Divides into the inferior thyroid, ascending cervical, transverse cervical and suprascapular arteries.
artery.thyrocervical-trunk.territory: Thyroid gland; posterior prevertebral muscles; trapezius and rhomboid muscles; posterior shoulder area.
verify: branches: the following names are given by the consulted sources but have no matching concept or record in the BP3D 4.0 release, and are carried as sourced text only: 'ascending cervical artery' - verify

artery.axillary-artery.course: Passes through the axilla deep to pectoralis minor within the axillary sheath; three parts relative to pectoralis minor (proximal, posterior, distal).
artery.axillary-artery.name: Axillary artery
artery.axillary-artery.origin: Continuation of the subclavian artery at the lateral border of the first rib.
artery.axillary-artery.termination: Becomes the brachial artery at the lower border of teres major.
artery.axillary-artery.territory: Axilla, pectoral region and shoulder; the circumflex humeral arteries form an anastomosis around the surgical neck of the humerus.

branches: the following names are given by the consulted sources but have no matching concept or record in the BP3D 4.0 release, and are carried as sourced text only: 'superior thoracic artery' - verify

artery.brachial-artery.course: Descends the arm with the median nerve, passing through the cubital fossa under the bicipital aponeurosis.
artery.brachial-artery.name: Brachial artery
artery.brachial-artery.origin: Continuation of the axillary artery at the lower border of teres major.
artery.brachial-artery.termination: Bifurcates into the radial and ulnar arteries in the cubital fossa.
verify: branches: the consulted source names the profunda brachii (deep artery of arm) as the principal branch; the ulnar collateral and muscular branches are not enumerated in the consulted sources - verify; note 'profunda brachii' has no concept in the BP3D release under that name - verify

artery.radial-artery.course: Descends the posterolateral forearm; palpable at the distal forearm lateral to the flexor carpi radialis tendon; enters the hand dorsally across the floor of the anatomical snuffbox.
artery.radial-artery.name: Radial artery
artery.radial-artery.origin: Formed by the bifurcation of the brachial artery in the cubital fossa.
artery.radial-artery.termination: Continues as the deep palmar arch in the hand.
artery.radial-artery.territory: Posterolateral aspect of the forearm; contributes to the deep palmar arch and to the superficial palmar arch.
verify: branches: radial recurrent, palmar carpal and superficial palmar branches are not enumerated in the consulted sources - verify

artery.ulnar-artery.course: Descends the anteromedial forearm; enters the hand anterior to the flexor retinaculum, lateral to the ulnar nerve.
artery.ulnar-artery.name: Ulnar artery
artery.ulnar-artery.origin: Formed by the bifurcation of the brachial artery in the cubital fossa.
artery.ulnar-artery.termination: Continues across the palm as the superficial palmar arch.
artery.ulnar-artery.territory: Anteromedial aspect of the forearm and the deeper forearm structures (via the interosseous arteries); forms the superficial palmar arch.

artery.celiac-artery.course: Short trunk (the coeliac trunk) dividing almost immediately into its three branches.
artery.celiac-artery.name: Celiac artery
artery.celiac-artery.origin: Large unpaired visceral branch of the abdominal aorta arising anteriorly at the level of T12.
artery.celiac-artery.termination: Trifurcates into the left gastric, splenic and common hepatic arteries.
artery.celiac-artery.territory: Foregut: liver, stomach, abdominal oesophagus, spleen, superior duodenum and superior pancreas.

artery.left-gastric-artery.course: Ascends to the gastro-oesophageal junction, giving oesophageal branches, then descends along the lesser curvature of the stomach in the lesser omentum.
artery.left-gastric-artery.name: Left gastric artery
artery.left-gastric-artery.origin: Smallest branch of the coeliac trunk.
artery.left-gastric-artery.termination: Anastomoses with the right gastric artery along the lesser curvature.
artery.left-gastric-artery.territory: Distal oesophagus and both surfaces of the stomach along the lesser curvature.

artery.splenic-artery.course: Takes a tortuous course to the left along the superior border of the pancreas, travels in the lienorenal ligament and divides into numerous branches entering the hilum of the spleen.
artery.splenic-artery.name: Splenic artery
artery.splenic-artery.origin: Largest branch of the coeliac trunk.
artery.splenic-artery.termination: Divides into terminal branches at the hilum of the spleen.
artery.splenic-artery.territory: Spleen; body and tail of the pancreas; fundus of the stomach (short gastric arteries); greater curvature of the stomach (left gastroepiploic artery).

artery.common-hepatic-artery.course: Runs to the right towards the liver.
artery.common-hepatic-artery.name: Common hepatic artery
artery.common-hepatic-artery.termination: Divides into its terminal branches, the hepatic artery proper and the gastroduodenal artery.
artery.common-hepatic-artery.territory: Liver (via the hepatic artery proper), gallbladder, stomach and duodenum/pancreatic head (via the gastroduodenal artery).

artery.hepatic-artery-proper.course: Ascends towards the liver in the free edge of the lesser omentum, to the left of the bile duct and anterior to the portal vein (portal triad).
artery.hepatic-artery-proper.name: Hepatic artery proper
artery.hepatic-artery-proper.origin: Terminal branch of the common hepatic artery, after the gastroduodenal artery is given off.
artery.hepatic-artery-proper.termination: Divides into the right and left hepatic arteries near the porta hepatis.

artery.gastroduodenal-artery.course: Travels behind the first part of the duodenum.
artery.gastroduodenal-artery.name: Gastroduodenal artery
artery.gastroduodenal-artery.note: The BP3D release carries this vessel as 'trunk of gastroduodenal artery'; the clinical record links that record.
artery.gastroduodenal-artery.origin: Terminal branch of the common hepatic artery.
artery.gastroduodenal-artery.termination: Splits into the right gastroepiploic and superior pancreaticoduodenal arteries.
artery.gastroduodenal-artery.territory: Superior part of the duodenum (to the major duodenal papilla) and the head and neck of the pancreas; greater curvature of the stomach via the right gastroepiploic artery.

artery.superior-mesenteric-artery.course: Runs in the root of the mesentery from the duodenojejunal flexure towards the ileocolic junction, crossing the third part of the duodenum.
artery.superior-mesenteric-artery.name: Superior mesenteric artery
artery.superior-mesenteric-artery.origin: Large unpaired visceral branch of the abdominal aorta arising anteriorly at the lower level of L1, just below the coeliac artery.
artery.superior-mesenteric-artery.termination: Ends at the ileocolic junction as the ileocolic artery.
artery.superior-mesenteric-artery.territory: Midgut: distal duodenum, jejuno-ileum, ascending colon and part of the transverse colon.

artery.inferior-mesenteric-artery.course: Descends on the left side of the abdominal aorta towards the pelvis.
artery.inferior-mesenteric-artery.name: Inferior mesenteric artery
artery.inferior-mesenteric-artery.origin: Large unpaired visceral branch of the abdominal aorta arising anteriorly at the level of L3.
artery.inferior-mesenteric-artery.termination: Continues as the superior rectal artery into the pelvis.
artery.inferior-mesenteric-artery.territory: Hindgut: large intestine from the splenic flexure to the upper part of the rectum.

artery.renal-artery.course: Passes laterally to the hilum of the kidney on each side.
artery.renal-artery.name: Renal artery
artery.renal-artery.origin: Paired visceral branches of the abdominal aorta arising laterally between L1 and L2.
artery.renal-artery.termination: Enters the kidney at the hilum, dividing into segmental branches.
verify: branches: the five segmental renal branches are named in the BP3D inventory as segmental artery records; their order is not enumerated in the consulted sources - verify

artery.common-iliac-artery.course: Descends into the pelvis on each side.
artery.common-iliac-artery.name: Common iliac artery
artery.common-iliac-artery.origin: Formed by the bifurcation of the abdominal aorta at the level of L4.
artery.common-iliac-artery.termination: Divides into the external and internal iliac arteries.

artery.external-iliac-artery.course: Descends along the pelvic brim and passes posterior to the inguinal ligament into the thigh.
artery.external-iliac-artery.name: External iliac artery
artery.external-iliac-artery.origin: Larger terminal branch of the common iliac artery.
artery.external-iliac-artery.termination: Becomes the femoral artery posterior to the inguinal ligament.
artery.external-iliac-artery.territory: The lower limb (as the femoral artery) and the lower abdominal wall.

artery.internal-iliac-artery.name: Internal iliac artery
artery.internal-iliac-artery.origin: Smaller terminal branch of the common iliac artery.
artery.internal-iliac-artery.territory: Pelvic organs, the gluteal region and the perineum.

artery.femoral-artery.course: Descends through the femoral triangle, then the adductor canal deep to sartorius, and exits through the adductor hiatus.
artery.femoral-artery.name: Femoral artery
artery.femoral-artery.origin: Continuation of the external iliac artery posterior to the inguinal ligament, at the mid-inguinal point.
artery.femoral-artery.termination: Becomes the popliteal artery after passing through the adductor hiatus.
artery.femoral-artery.territory: Lower abdominal wall, thigh and external genitalia (via its branches); the principal artery of the lower limb.

artery.popliteal-artery.course: Runs through the popliteal fossa as its deepest structure, close to the capsule of the knee joint.
artery.popliteal-artery.name: Popliteal artery
artery.popliteal-artery.origin: Continuation of the femoral artery after the adductor hiatus.
artery.popliteal-artery.termination: Ends at the lower border of popliteus by dividing into the anterior and posterior tibial arteries.
artery.popliteal-artery.territory: Knee region (via genicular branches) and, through its terminal branches, the leg and foot.

artery.anterior-tibial-artery.course: Passes through the interosseous membrane into the anterior compartment of the leg and descends with the deep peroneal (fibular) nerve.
artery.anterior-tibial-artery.name: Anterior tibial artery
artery.anterior-tibial-artery.origin: Smaller terminal branch of the popliteal artery.
artery.anterior-tibial-artery.termination: Becomes the dorsalis pedis (dorsal artery of the foot) at the ankle joint, midway between the malleoli.
artery.anterior-tibial-artery.territory: Structures of the anterior compartment of the leg and the dorsum of the foot.

artery.posterior-tibial-artery.course: Descends in the posterior compartment of the leg and passes posterior to the medial malleolus into the sole of the foot.
artery.posterior-tibial-artery.name: Posterior tibial artery
artery.posterior-tibial-artery.origin: Larger terminal branch of the popliteal artery.
artery.posterior-tibial-artery.termination: Divides into the medial and lateral plantar arteries in the sole of the foot.
artery.posterior-tibial-artery.territory: Posterior compartment of the leg and the sole of the foot.

artery.pulmonary-artery.note: The pulmonary trunk itself is carried in the inventory within the pulmonary artery records; consulted sources describe the trunk dividing into the two pulmonary arteries.
artery.pulmonary-artery.origin: The pulmonary trunk arises from the right ventricle through the pulmonary semilunar valve and divides into the right and left pulmonary arteries.

vein.superior-vena-cava.course: Descends vertically in the superior mediastinum.
vein.superior-vena-cava.name: Superior vena cava
vein.superior-vena-cava.origin: Formed by the union of the right and left brachiocephalic veins behind the right first costal cartilage.
vein.superior-vena-cava.termination: Drains into the right atrium of the heart.
vein.superior-vena-cava.territory: Head, neck, thorax (above the diaphragm, except the heart wall) and upper limbs.

vein.inferior-vena-cava.course: Ascends on the posterior abdominal wall, anterior to the vertebral column and to the right of the abdominal aorta; leaves the abdomen through the caval hiatus of the diaphragm at T8.
vein.inferior-vena-cava.name: Inferior vena cava
vein.inferior-vena-cava.origin: Formed by the union of the common iliac veins at the level of L5.
vein.inferior-vena-cava.termination: Drains into the right atrium of the heart.

vein.brachiocephalic-vein.course: Right: descends vertically (about 2.5 cm). Left: crosses obliquely behind the sternum (about 6 cm).
vein.brachiocephalic-vein.name: Brachiocephalic vein
vein.brachiocephalic-vein.origin: Formed on each side by the union of the internal jugular vein and the subclavian vein, posterior to the sternoclavicular joint.
vein.brachiocephalic-vein.termination: The two brachiocephalic veins unite to form the superior vena cava.
vein.brachiocephalic-vein.territory: Head, neck and upper limb of its side.

vein.internal-jugular-vein.course: Descends through the neck in the carotid sheath, beside the internal carotid and then the common carotid artery.
vein.internal-jugular-vein.name: Internal jugular vein
vein.internal-jugular-vein.origin: Begins at the jugular foramen as the continuation of the sigmoid sinus (dural venous sinus).
vein.internal-jugular-vein.termination: Joins the subclavian vein behind the sternal end of the clavicle to form the brachiocephalic vein.
vein.internal-jugular-vein.territory: The brain (via the dural venous sinuses), face and neck; the largest vein draining the head and neck.

vein.external-jugular-vein.note: Clinical text only in v1: the vessel itself is absent from the source tables. See MILESTONE-5.md.
vein.external-jugular-vein.territory: Superficial parts of the scalp and face.

vein.subclavian-vein.course: Runs from the outer border of the first rib to the medial border of the anterior scalene muscle, anterior to the muscle.
vein.subclavian-vein.name: Subclavian vein
vein.subclavian-vein.origin: Continuation of the axillary vein at the outer border of the first rib.
vein.subclavian-vein.termination: Joins the internal jugular vein to form the brachiocephalic vein.
vein.subclavian-vein.territory: The upper limb; also receives the external jugular vein (scalp and face).
verify: branches: the following names are given by the consulted sources but have no matching concept or record in the BP3D 4.0 release, and are carried as sourced text only: 'external jugular vein' - verify

vein.axillary-vein.course: Ascends through the axilla with the axillary artery.
vein.axillary-vein.name: Axillary vein
vein.axillary-vein.termination: Becomes the subclavian vein at the outer border of the first rib.
verify: origin: formation (continuation of the brachial veins / basilic vein junction) is not stated in the consulted sources - verify
branches: tributaries not enumerated in the consulted sources - verify

vein.azygos-vein.course: Enters the thorax through the aortic hiatus, ascends along the right side of the thoracic vertebral bodies, and arches anteriorly over the root of the right lung at T4.
vein.azygos-vein.name: Azygos vein
vein.azygos-vein.origin: Formed by the union of the right ascending lumbar vein and the right subcostal vein at the level of T12.
vein.azygos-vein.termination: Empties into the superior vena cava.
vein.azygos-vein.territory: Posterior walls of the thorax and abdomen; the azygos system also connects the superior and inferior caval systems.
verify: branches: the following names are given by the consulted sources but have no matching concept or record in the BP3D 4.0 release, and are carried as sourced text only: 'right posterior intercostal vein'; 'esophageal vein'; 'mediastinal vein'; 'right bronchial vein' - verify

vein.hemiazygos-vein.course: Ascends on the left side of the vertebral column to about T8-T9, then crosses the vertebral column posterior to the aorta, oesophagus and thoracic duct.
vein.hemiazygos-vein.name: Hemiazygos vein
vein.hemiazygos-vein.origin: Formed by the union of the left ascending lumbar vein and the left subcostal vein.
vein.hemiazygos-vein.territory: Lower left posterolateral chest wall (left posterior intercostal veins 9-11).
verify: branches: the following names are given by the consulted sources but have no matching concept or record in the BP3D 4.0 release, and are carried as sourced text only: 'left posterior intercostal vein'; 'esophageal vein'; 'mediastinal vein' - verify

vein.accessory-hemiazygos-vein.course: Descends along the left side of the vertebral column and crosses to the right at about T7-T8.
vein.accessory-hemiazygos-vein.name: Accessory hemiazygos vein
vein.accessory-hemiazygos-vein.origin: Begins at the 4th or 5th intercostal space as the continuation of the left fourth posterior intercostal vein.
vein.accessory-hemiazygos-vein.termination: Joins the azygos vein (or the hemiazygos vein).
vein.accessory-hemiazygos-vein.territory: Mid levels of the left posterolateral chest wall (left posterior intercostal veins 4-8).
verify: branches: the following names are given by the consulted sources but have no matching concept or record in the BP3D 4.0 release, and are carried as sourced text only: 'left posterior intercostal vein'; 'left bronchial vein' - verify

vein.coronary-sinus.course: Runs in the posterior coronary sulcus of the heart.
vein.coronary-sinus.name: Coronary sinus
vein.coronary-sinus.note: The coronary sinus is a PART-OF-only concept in the BP3D release (venous trunk line); its record is the partof-concept inventory record.
vein.coronary-sinus.termination: Empties directly into the right atrium.
vein.coronary-sinus.territory: The wall of the heart (most of its venous drainage gathers here).

vein.common-iliac-vein.course: Ascends in the pelvis to the level of L5.
vein.common-iliac-vein.name: Common iliac vein
vein.common-iliac-vein.origin: Formed by the union of the external iliac and internal iliac veins.
vein.common-iliac-vein.termination: The two common iliac veins unite to form the inferior vena cava at L5.
vein.common-iliac-vein.territory: The lower limb and the gluteal region (and the pelvic viscera via the internal iliac vein).

vein.external-iliac-vein.name: External iliac vein
vein.external-iliac-vein.origin: Continuation of the femoral vein posterior to the inguinal ligament.
vein.external-iliac-vein.termination: Joins the internal iliac vein to form the common iliac vein.

vein.internal-iliac-vein.name: Internal iliac vein
vein.internal-iliac-vein.termination: Joins the external iliac vein to form the common iliac vein.
vein.internal-iliac-vein.territory: Pelvic viscera and the gluteal region.

vein.renal-vein.course: Passes medially to join the inferior vena cava; the left renal vein is longer and crosses between the aorta and the superior mesenteric artery.
vein.renal-vein.name: Renal vein
vein.renal-vein.origin: Formed at the hilum of the kidney.
vein.renal-vein.termination: Drains into the inferior vena cava.
vein.renal-vein.territory: The kidney; on the left also the left adrenal gland and the left testis/ovary (via the left suprarenal and left gonadal veins).

vein.hepatic-vein.course: Ascends within the liver to the inferior vena cava just below the diaphragm.
vein.hepatic-vein.name: Hepatic vein
vein.hepatic-vein.note: Venous return from the spleen, pancreas, gallbladder and GI tract reaches the IVC via the hepatic veins after passing through the portal system (S4).
vein.hepatic-vein.origin: Formed within the liver parenchyma from the central veins of the lobules.
vein.hepatic-vein.termination: Drains into the inferior vena cava.
vein.hepatic-vein.territory: The liver (its entire venous outflow, including portal blood after processing).
verify: branches: the middle hepatic vein is carried in the BP3D inventory within the lateralised hepatic vein records; the consulted source does not enumerate three named trunks - verify

vein.femoral-vein.course: Ascends the thigh anteriorly, accompanying the femoral artery.
vein.femoral-vein.name: Femoral vein
vein.femoral-vein.origin: Continuation of the popliteal vein as it enters the thigh via the adductor canal.
vein.femoral-vein.termination: Becomes the external iliac vein posterior to the inguinal ligament.
vein.femoral-vein.territory: The lower limb (deep structures of the thigh and leg, plus the superficial drainage via the great saphenous vein).
verify: branches: 'deep vein of thigh' (profunda femoris vein) is named in S5; its record linkage follows the femoral records - verify

vein.popliteal-vein.course: Ascends through the popliteal fossa and enters the thigh via the adductor canal.
vein.popliteal-vein.name: Popliteal vein
vein.popliteal-vein.origin: Formed on the posterior surface of the knee by the union of the anterior tibial, posterior tibial and fibular veins.
vein.popliteal-vein.termination: Continues as the femoral vein on entering the thigh.
vein.popliteal-vein.territory: The leg and foot (deep veins) and the posterior leg (via the small saphenous vein).

vein.great-saphenous-vein.course: Ascends the medial side of the leg, passing anterior to the medial malleolus at the ankle and posterior to the medial condyle at the knee, then up the medial thigh.
vein.great-saphenous-vein.name: Great saphenous vein
vein.great-saphenous-vein.note: Harvested as a graft in coronary artery bypass surgery (S5 flashcards set; recorded as clinical context).
vein.great-saphenous-vein.origin: Formed by the dorsal venous arch of the foot and the dorsal vein of the great toe.
vein.great-saphenous-vein.termination: Drains into the femoral vein immediately inferior to the inguinal ligament.
vein.great-saphenous-vein.territory: Superficial tissues of the medial leg and thigh (the longest vein in the body).
verify: branches: named tributaries near the saphenofemoral junction are not enumerated in the consulted sources - verify

vein.small-saphenous-vein.course: Ascends the posterior side of the leg, passing posterior to the lateral malleolus along the lateral border of the calcaneal tendon.
vein.small-saphenous-vein.name: Small saphenous vein
vein.small-saphenous-vein.origin: Formed by the dorsal venous arch of the foot and the dorsal vein of the little toe.
vein.small-saphenous-vein.termination: Passes between the two heads of gastrocnemius and empties into the popliteal vein in the popliteal fossa.
vein.small-saphenous-vein.territory: Superficial tissues of the posterior leg.
verify: branches: tributaries not enumerated in the consulted sources - verify

vein.pulmonary-vein.course: Passes from the hilum of each lung to the left atrium.
vein.pulmonary-vein.name: Pulmonary vein
vein.pulmonary-vein.note: Anatomy has four pulmonary veins (superior and inferior on each side), as stated in S10; the BP3D release carries the pulmonary veins only as one undivided family concept.
vein.pulmonary-vein.origin: Arises within the lung parenchyma from the pulmonary capillary networks.
vein.pulmonary-vein.termination: Opens into the left atrium (four pulmonary veins in the usual pattern).
vein.pulmonary-vein.territory: The lungs (oxygenated blood returning to the heart).

vein.hepatic-portal-vein.course: Ascends posterior to the superior part of the duodenum and the bile duct, within the hepatoduodenal ligament.
vein.hepatic-portal-vein.name: Hepatic portal vein
vein.hepatic-portal-vein.origin: Formed by the union of the splenic vein and the superior mesenteric vein, posterior to the neck of the pancreas at the level of L2.
vein.hepatic-portal-vein.termination: Divides into right and left branches at the porta hepatis, which enter the liver parenchyma separately.
vein.hepatic-portal-vein.territory: Venous drainage of the spleen, pancreas, gallbladder and the abdominal part of the gastrointestinal tract, carried to the liver for processing; the portal vein provides about three-fourths of the liver's blood supply.

vein.splenic-vein.course: Runs straight across the posterior abdominal wall in contact with the body of the pancreas, to the neck of the pancreas.
vein.splenic-vein.name: Splenic vein
vein.splenic-vein.origin: Formed from a number of smaller vessels as they leave the hilum of the spleen.
vein.splenic-vein.termination: Joins the superior mesenteric vein behind the neck of the pancreas to form the portal vein.
vein.splenic-vein.territory: Spleen, fundus and greater curvature of the stomach, pancreas, and (via the inferior mesenteric vein) the hindgut colon.
verify: branches: the following names are given by the consulted sources but have no matching concept or record in the BP3D 4.0 release, and are carried as sourced text only: 'short gastric vein'; 'pancreatic vein' - verify

vein.superior-mesenteric-vein.course: Ascends within the mesentery of the small intestine to the neck of the pancreas.
vein.superior-mesenteric-vein.name: Superior mesenteric vein
vein.superior-mesenteric-vein.origin: Begins in the right iliac fossa as the convergence of the veins draining the terminal ileum, caecum and appendix.
vein.superior-mesenteric-vein.termination: Joins the splenic vein behind the neck of the pancreas to form the portal vein.
vein.superior-mesenteric-vein.territory: Small intestine, caecum, ascending colon and transverse colon.
verify: branches: the following names are given by the consulted sources but have no matching concept or record in the BP3D 4.0 release, and are carried as sourced text only: 'inferior pancreaticoduodenal vein'; 'jejunal vein' - verify

vein.inferior-mesenteric-vein.course: Ascends, receiving the sigmoid and left colic veins, and passes posterior to the body of the pancreas.
vein.inferior-mesenteric-vein.name: Inferior mesenteric vein
vein.inferior-mesenteric-vein.origin: Begins as the superior rectal vein in the pelvis.
vein.inferior-mesenteric-vein.territory: Rectum, sigmoid colon, descending colon and splenic flexure.

variant.replaced-right-hepatic-artery-fr.clinical_significance: At risk in cholecystectomy, pancreaticoduodenectomy and liver transplantation; the most common hepatic arterial variant and the chief variant source of bile-duct blood supply (S14).
variant.replaced-right-hepatic-artery-fr.description: The right hepatic artery arises from the superior mesenteric artery instead of the hepatic artery proper, and classically ascends posterolateral to the common bile duct, posterior to the main portal vein.
variant.replaced-right-hepatic-artery-fr.name: Replaced right hepatic artery arising from the superior mesenteric artery (Michels type III)

prevalence.basis: Michels type III range in S13

variant.replaced-right-hepatic-artery-fr.unmodeled_note: Prevalence recorded per the variant gate; variant geometry is not modelled in v1 (the BP3D release carries the standard pattern only).

variant.replaced-left-hepatic-artery-fro.clinical_significance: At risk in gastrectomy and hepatobiliary surgery; may be the sole supply to the left lobe.
variant.replaced-left-hepatic-artery-fro.description: The left hepatic artery arises from the left gastric artery and reaches the liver through the lesser omentum / fissure for the ligamentum venosum.
variant.replaced-left-hepatic-artery-fro.name: Replaced left hepatic artery arising from the left gastric artery (Michels type II)

prevalence.basis: pooled 3.0% in S14; 10% in the Michels table of S15

variant.replaced-left-hepatic-artery-fro.unmodeled_note: Prevalence recorded per the variant gate; variant geometry is not modelled in v1.

variant.accessory-left-hepatic-artery-fr.clinical_significance: At risk in gastrectomy; division can compromise left-lobe perfusion where it is dominant.
variant.accessory-left-hepatic-artery-fr.description: An accessory left hepatic artery from the left gastric artery supplements (does not replace) the normal left hepatic artery.
variant.accessory-left-hepatic-artery-fr.name: Accessory left hepatic artery arising from the left gastric artery (Michels type V)
variant.accessory-left-hepatic-artery-fr.unmodeled_note: Prevalence recorded per the variant gate; variant geometry is not modelled in v1.

variant.accessory-right-hepatic-artery-f.clinical_significance: At risk in pancreatic and hepatobiliary surgery.
variant.accessory-right-hepatic-artery-f.description: An accessory right hepatic artery from the superior mesenteric artery supplements the normal right hepatic artery.
variant.accessory-right-hepatic-artery-f.name: Accessory right hepatic artery arising from the superior mesenteric artery (Michels type VI)

prevalence.basis: Michels type VI range in S13

variant.accessory-right-hepatic-artery-f.unmodeled_note: Prevalence recorded per the variant gate; variant geometry is not modelled in v1.

variant.common-hepatic-artery-from-sma.clinical_significance: Load-bearing in pancreaticoduodenectomy planning and coeliac-axis intervention.
variant.common-hepatic-artery-from-sma.description: The entire common hepatic artery arises from the superior mesenteric artery (hepatomesenteric trunk pattern).
variant.common-hepatic-artery-from-sma.name: Common hepatic artery arising from the superior mesenteric artery (Michels type IX)

prevalence.basis: Michels type IX range in S13

variant.common-hepatic-artery-from-sma.unmodeled_note: Prevalence recorded per the variant gate; variant geometry is not modelled in v1.

variant.coronary-dominance-right.clinical_significance: Determines the territory at risk in right coronary occlusion and the interpretation of coronary angiography.
variant.coronary-dominance-right.description: The posterior descending (posterior interventricular) artery originates from the right coronary artery.
variant.coronary-dominance-right.name: Right coronary dominance

variant.coronary-dominance-left.clinical_significance: Circumflex occlusion in left dominance jeopardises the inferior wall and the AV node supply.
variant.coronary-dominance-left.description: The posterior descending artery originates from the left circumflex artery.
variant.coronary-dominance-left.name: Left coronary dominance
variant.coronary-dominance-left.unmodeled_note: Prevalence recorded per the variant gate; the v1 coronary records describe the right-dominant pattern, with the variant origin stated on the posterior interventricular record.

variant.coronary-dominance-codominant.clinical_significance: Shared inferior-wall supply; relevant to angiographic interpretation.
variant.coronary-dominance-codominant.description: The posterior descending artery is supplied by both the right coronary artery and the left circumflex artery.
variant.coronary-dominance-codominant.name: Coronary codominance
variant.coronary-dominance-codominant.unmodeled_note: Prevalence recorded per the variant gate; variant geometry is not modelled in v1.

central.cerebellum.name: Cerebellum
central.cerebellum.function: Processes input from the premotor cortex, brain stem and sensory receptors to provide feedback for precise, coordinated movements of skeletal muscles; plays a major role in balance (S8).
central.cerebellum.connections: Connected to the brain stem by three paired peduncles: inferior (to the medulla, conveying sensory/proprioceptive input), middle (the ventral pons, conveying a copy of cortical motor commands) and superior (to the midbrain and thalamus, its major output) (S8).
central.cerebellum.note: Comprises about 10-11% of brain mass and lies dorsal to the pons and medulla (S8). The release names no cerebellar nucleus, vermis or flocculus (probe-verified absences); the record's geometry is the whole-organ composition only.

central.brainstem.connections: Continuous cranially with the diencephalon and caudally, via the medulla, with the spinal cord at the foramen magnum (S8).
central.brainstem.note: Consists of the midbrain, pons and medulla oblongata (S8). In the release the brainstem concept hangs in the PART-OF tree under head proper, not under the nervous system (see inventory).

central.midbrain.name: Midbrain

organ.brain.name: Brain
organ.brain.parts: Cerebrum (two cerebral hemispheres, each with frontal, parietal, temporal and occipital lobes), cerebellum, brainstem (midbrain, pons, medulla oblongata) and diencephalon (thalamus, hypothalamus and associated structures).

organ.spinal-cord.name: Spinal cord
organ.spinal-cord.segments: 31 segments: 8 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral and 1 coccygeal, each giving origin to a pair of spinal nerves (S10). Each spinal nerve forms from an anterior (motor) and a posterior (sensory) root uniting at the intervertebral foramen, then divides into posterior and anterior rami (S9).
organ.spinal-cord.structure: Arises cranially as a continuation of the medulla oblongata and travels within the vertebral canal surrounded by the spinal meninges (dura mater, arachnoid mater, pia mater). At the L2 vertebral level it tapers to the conus medullaris; the spinal nerves arising beyond it form the cauda equina. Two enlargements: cervical (C4-T1, origin of the brachial plexus) and lumbar (T11-L1, origin of the lumbar and sacral plexi). Distally the meninges form the filum terminale, anchoring the cord to the coccyx (S9).
organ.spinal-cord.arterial_supply: Three longitudinal arteries: the anterior spinal artery (from the vertebral arteries) and the paired posterior spinal arteries (from the vertebral artery or the posteroinferior cerebellar artery), reinforced by anterior and posterior segmental medullary arteries; the largest, the artery of Adamkiewicz, supplies the inferior two thirds of the cord (S9).

meninges: the release carries no pia mater or arachnoid mater concept and only class concepts for the dura (region of dura mater; subdivision of cranial dura mater) plus the tentorium cerebelli; the three membranes named by S9 are therefore not modelled - verify

major.cn-01-olfactory.name: Olfactory nerve (CN I)
major.cn-01-olfactory.root_values: Arises from the cerebrum — one of the two cranial nerves that do not arise from the brainstem; its fibres are the axons of the olfactory receptor neurons of the nasal epithelium, which project to the olfactory bulb.
major.cn-01-olfactory.course: From the olfactory epithelium of the nasal cavity, the nerve fibres pass upward through the cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone to the olfactory bulb.
major.cn-01-olfactory.motor_distribution: None — the nerve is purely sensory (special visceral sensory, SVS).
major.cn-01-olfactory.clinical_testing: Tested by presenting common smells (for example coffee or mint) to one nostril at a time; the patient should be able to recognise the smell. Loss of the sense of smell is anosmia, which can follow blunt head trauma if all the fibres are sheared as the brain moves within the cranium.
major.cn-01-olfactory.note: Links the sided FMA 5.1.0 concept records named in geometry_record_ids; those records are geometry-absent — the FMA is an ontology and carries no mesh data (Milestone 33).

major.cn-02-optic.name: Optic nerve (CN II)
major.cn-02-optic.root_values: Arises from the cerebrum; the nerve carries the axons of the retina — including the photosensitive ganglion cells that send the signal for the pupillary light response — to the brain.
major.cn-02-optic.course: From the retina, the nerve enters the cranium through the optic canal and meets its fellow at the optic chiasm, where fibres sort so that the two halves of the visual field are processed by opposite sides of the brain.
major.cn-02-optic.motor_distribution: None — the nerve is purely sensory (special somatic sensory, SSS).
major.cn-02-optic.clinical_testing: Visual acuity is tested with a Snellen chart; the extent of the visual field is tested by establishing the boundaries of peripheral vision; the optic disk, where the optic nerve emerges from the eye, is inspected through the pupil with an ophthalmoscope. The nerve is the afferent (sensory) limb of the pupillary light reflex. Loss of peripheral vision ('tunnel vision') may result from a pituitary tumour pressing on the optic chiasm.
major.cn-02-optic.note: Links the BodyParts3D 4.0 inventory records named in geometry_record_ids, which carry geometry in the nervous system module (Milestone 9).

major.cn-03-oculomotor.name: Oculomotor nerve (CN III)
major.cn-03-oculomotor.root_values: Arises at the midbrain–pontine junction of the brainstem.
major.cn-03-oculomotor.course: From the midbrain–pontine junction, the nerve passes to the orbit and enters it through the superior orbital fissure.
major.cn-03-oculomotor.motor_distribution: Somatic motor (GSM): four extrinsic eye muscles — superior rectus, inferior rectus, medial rectus and inferior oblique (all the extraocular muscles except lateral rectus and superior oblique) — and the levator palpebrae superioris. Visceral motor (GVM, parasympathetic): the pupillary sphincter, and control of the shape of the lens for accommodation.
major.cn-03-oculomotor.sensory_distribution: None — the nerve is motor only (general somatic motor and general visceral motor).
major.cn-03-oculomotor.clinical_testing: Eye movement is tested by having the patient track the tip of a pen through the visual field, watching for conjugate movement; failure of one eye to move in conjugation with the other produces diplopia. Moving the pen in toward the face tests convergence and accommodation. The nerve is the efferent (motor) limb of the pupillary light reflex: if light in either eye elicits constriction in only one eye, the problem is with the oculomotor system.
major.cn-03-oculomotor.note: Links the sided FMA 5.1.0 concept records named in geometry_record_ids; those records are geometry-absent — the FMA is an ontology and carries no mesh data (Milestone 33).

major.cn-04-trochlear.name: Trochlear nerve (CN IV)
major.cn-04-trochlear.root_values: Arises from the posterior side of the midbrain; it has the longest intracranial length of all the cranial nerves.
major.cn-04-trochlear.course: From the posterior midbrain, the nerve travels to the orbit and enters it through the superior orbital fissure.
major.cn-04-trochlear.motor_distribution: The superior oblique muscle (general somatic motor), which rotates the eye along its axis medially (intorsion).
major.cn-04-trochlear.sensory_distribution: None — the nerve is motor only (general somatic motor).
major.cn-04-trochlear.clinical_testing: Tested with the other gaze nerves by having the patient track the tip of a pen through the visual field, watching for conjugate movement; failure of the superior oblique to act in conjugation with the other eye produces diplopia.
major.cn-04-trochlear.note: Links the BodyParts3D 4.0 inventory records named in geometry_record_ids, which carry geometry in the nervous system module (Milestone 9).

major.cn-05-trigeminal.name: Trigeminal nerve (CN V)
major.cn-05-trigeminal.course: From the pons, the nerve divides into three divisions that leave the cranium separately: the ophthalmic division through the superior orbital fissure, the maxillary division through the foramen rotundum, and the mandibular division through the foramen ovale.
major.cn-05-trigeminal.motor_distribution: The muscles of mastication (special visceral motor, via the mandibular division).
major.cn-05-trigeminal.sensory_distribution: General sensation (GSS) from the face and head, by division — ophthalmic: scalp, forehead and nose; maxillary: cheeks, lower eyelid, nasal mucosa, upper lip, upper teeth and palate; mandibular: anterior two-thirds of the tongue (general sensation), skin over the mandible and lower teeth.
major.cn-05-trigeminal.clinical_testing: Sensory function is tested by discrimination on the face: while the patient's eyes are closed, the examiner alternates the cotton tip (light touch) and the snapped pointed end (pain) of a cotton-tipped applicator, and the patient identifies whether the stimulus is sharp or dull. The nerve is also the sensory component of the jaw-jerk reflex, via its mesencephalic nucleus, which processes proprioceptive information of the face.
major.cn-05-trigeminal.note: Links the sided FMA 5.1.0 concept records named in geometry_record_ids; those records are geometry-absent — the FMA is an ontology and carries no mesh data (Milestone 33).

major.cn-06-abducens.name: Abducens nerve (CN VI)
major.cn-06-abducens.root_values: Arises at the pontine–medulla junction of the brainstem.
major.cn-06-abducens.course: From the pontine–medulla junction, the nerve passes to the orbit and enters it through the superior orbital fissure.
major.cn-06-abducens.motor_distribution: The lateral rectus muscle (general somatic motor), which abducts the eye.
major.cn-06-abducens.sensory_distribution: None — the nerve is motor only (general somatic motor).
major.cn-06-abducens.clinical_testing: Tested by having the patient track the tip of a pen through the visual field: in horizontal gaze the lateral rectus of one eye acts with the medial rectus of the other. Failure of one eye to abduct while the other adducts is internuclear ophthalmoplegia, and diplopia results from any failure of the extraocular muscles to move one eye in perfect conjugation with the other.
major.cn-06-abducens.note: Links the sided FMA 5.1.0 concept records named in geometry_record_ids; those records are geometry-absent — the FMA is an ontology and carries no mesh data (Milestone 33).

major.cn-07-facial.name: Facial nerve (CN VII)
major.cn-07-facial.root_values: Arises at the pontine–medulla junction of the brainstem.
major.cn-07-facial.course: From the pontine–medulla junction, the nerve enters the internal acoustic meatus and ultimately leaves the skull through the stylomastoid foramen.
major.cn-07-facial.motor_distribution: The muscles of facial expression (special visceral motor). Visceral motor (GVM, parasympathetic): the lacrimal gland, the submandibular and sublingual glands, and the mucous glands of the mouth and nose.
major.cn-07-facial.sensory_distribution: Taste from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue and from the hard and soft palates (special visceral sensory); general sensation from part of the external ear (GSS).
major.cn-07-facial.clinical_testing: Taste is tested by introducing salty, sour, bitter or sweet stimuli to either side of the tongue. The muscles of facial expression are tested by directed contraction against resistance — for example, the patient squeezes her eyes shut while the examiner tries to pry them open; the muscles of the upper and lower face both need to be tested, and severe deficits are obvious as one side of the face not moving like the other.
major.cn-07-facial.note: Links the sided FMA 5.1.0 concept records named in geometry_record_ids; those records are geometry-absent — the FMA is an ontology and carries no mesh data (Milestone 33).

major.cn-08-vestibulocochlear.name: Vestibulocochlear nerve (CN VIII)
major.cn-08-vestibulocochlear.root_values: Arises at the pontine–medulla junction; its vestibular and cochlear divisions carry equilibrium and auditory sensations from the inner ear to the medulla.
major.cn-08-vestibulocochlear.course: The two divisions emerge from the inner ear, pass through the internal auditory (acoustic) meatus, and synapse in nuclei of the superior medulla.
major.cn-08-vestibulocochlear.motor_distribution: None — the nerve is purely sensory (special somatic sensory, SSS).
major.cn-08-vestibulocochlear.sensory_distribution: Hearing (cochlear division) and balance / equilibrium (vestibular division) (special somatic sensory).
major.cn-08-vestibulocochlear.clinical_testing: Hearing is tested with a tuning fork: in the Rinne test the vibrating fork is placed on the mastoid process until the sound is no longer heard, then moved beside the ear canal — if the sound is then not heard, a conductive hearing deficit is present; in the Weber test the fork is placed on top of the skull, and with unilateral conductive loss the sound is louder in the affected ear, while with unilateral sensorineural loss it is quieter in that ear. Equilibrium is assessed through the vestibulo-ocular reflex. Ménière's disease can affect both systems, with vertigo, a low-frequency ringing in the ears, or a loss of hearing.
major.cn-08-vestibulocochlear.note: Links the sided FMA 5.1.0 concept records named in geometry_record_ids; those records are geometry-absent — the FMA is an ontology and carries no mesh data (Milestone 33).

major.cn-09-glossopharyngeal.name: Glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX)
major.cn-09-glossopharyngeal.root_values: Arises from the medulla oblongata, posterior to the olive.
major.cn-09-glossopharyngeal.course: From the medulla, the nerve leaves the cranium through the jugular foramen.
major.cn-09-glossopharyngeal.motor_distribution: The stylopharyngeus muscle (special visceral motor). Visceral motor (GVM, parasympathetic): the parotid gland, via fibres that synapse in the otic ganglion.
major.cn-09-glossopharyngeal.sensory_distribution: Taste from the posterior one-third of the tongue (SVS); general sensation from the posterior one-third of the tongue, part of the external ear and the middle ear cavity (GSS); visceral sensation from the carotid body and carotid sinus (GVS).
major.cn-09-glossopharyngeal.clinical_testing: The nerve relays general sensation from the pharyngeal walls and forms the afferent limb of the gag reflex: moving a tongue depressor to contact the lateral wall of the fauces should elicit the gag reflex, and stimulation of either side should elicit an equivalent response. Taste from the posterior tongue is tested with salty, sour, bitter or sweet stimuli applied to the tongue.
major.cn-09-glossopharyngeal.note: Links the sided FMA 5.1.0 concept records named in geometry_record_ids; those records are geometry-absent — the FMA is an ontology and carries no mesh data (Milestone 33).

major.cn-10-vagus.name: Vagus nerve (CN X)
major.cn-10-vagus.root_values: Arises from the medulla oblongata, posterior to the olive.
major.cn-10-vagus.course: From the medulla, the nerve leaves the cranium through the jugular foramen and descends through the neck; it has autonomic functions in the thoracic and superior abdominal cavities.
major.cn-10-vagus.motor_distribution: Most muscles of the pharynx and larynx (special visceral motor) — the vagus directly stimulates the contraction of skeletal muscles in the pharynx and larynx to contribute to the swallowing and speech functions; smooth muscle of the pharynx, larynx and most of the gastrointestinal tract (general visceral motor).
major.cn-10-vagus.sensory_distribution: Visceral sensation from the larynx, pharynx and the thoracic and abdominal viscera (GVS); general sensation from part of the external ear, the larynx and the pharynx (GSS); taste from the epiglottis region of the tongue (SVS).
major.cn-10-vagus.clinical_testing: Motor function is tested through the gag reflex — the motor response, contraction of the muscles of the pharynx, is mediated through the vagus nerve — and by having the patient repeat consonant sounds such as 'lah-kah-pah' while the examiner observes the movements of the soft palate and the arches between the palate and the tongue.
major.cn-10-vagus.note: Links the sided FMA 5.1.0 concept records named in geometry_record_ids; those records are geometry-absent — the FMA is an ontology and carries no mesh data (Milestone 33).

major.cn-11-accessory.name: Accessory nerve (CN XI)
major.cn-11-accessory.root_values: Cranial root from the medulla (nucleus ambiguus); spinal root from the upper cervical spinal cord.
major.cn-11-accessory.course: The spinal root ascends and enters the cranial cavity through the foramen magnum; the nerve then exits the skull through the jugular foramen to reach the sternocleidomastoid and trapezius.
major.cn-11-accessory.motor_distribution: The sternocleidomastoid and trapezius muscles (general somatic motor); a few fibres run with the vagus nerve to the viscera (special visceral motor).
major.cn-11-accessory.sensory_distribution: None — the nerve is motor only.
major.cn-11-accessory.clinical_testing: Tested by asking the patient to shrug both shoulders against resistance (trapezius) and to flex and extend the neck, or laterally flex the neck toward the shoulder, against resistance (sternocleidomastoid and trapezius); any difference on one side versus the other would suggest damage on the weaker side.
major.cn-11-accessory.note: Links the sided FMA 5.1.0 concept records named in geometry_record_ids; those records are geometry-absent — the FMA is an ontology and carries no mesh data (Milestone 33). ta_name/ta_code follow the linked FMA records' Milestone 35 outcome (TA2 6356, nervus accessorius spinalis); the Milestone 9 whole-nerve clinical record (nerve.cn-11-accessory) carries the Milestone 23 outcome TA2 6352, nervus accessorius.

major.cn-12-hypoglossal.name: Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)
major.cn-12-hypoglossal.root_values: Arises from the medulla oblongata, anterior to the olive.
major.cn-12-hypoglossal.course: From the medulla, the nerve leaves the cranium through the hypoglossal canal and passes to the tongue.
major.cn-12-hypoglossal.motor_distribution: The intrinsic and extrinsic muscles of the tongue (general somatic motor), except the palatoglossus, which is controlled by the vagus nerve.
major.cn-12-hypoglossal.sensory_distribution: None — the nerve is motor only (general somatic motor).
major.cn-12-hypoglossal.clinical_testing: Tested by asking the patient to stick out the tongue: the genioglossus is responsible for protrusion, so if the nerve on one side has a deficit, the tongue sticks out toward the side with the damage. Loss of function of the tongue can interfere with speech and swallowing.
major.cn-12-hypoglossal.note: Links the sided FMA 5.1.0 concept records named in geometry_record_ids; those records are geometry-absent — the FMA is an ontology and carries no mesh data (Milestone 33).

major.superior-trunk.name: Superior trunk of brachial plexus
major.superior-trunk.root_values: Formed by the union of the anterior rami of C5 and C6; the roots emerge between the anterior and middle scalene muscles.
major.superior-trunk.course: The trunk traverses the posterior triangle of the neck and divides into anterior and posterior divisions, which go on to form the cords of the plexus.
major.superior-trunk.motor_distribution: Gives off the suprascapular nerve (to supraspinatus and infraspinatus) and the nerve to subclavius; its fibres continue via the lateral and posterior cords into the terminal nerves of the upper limb.
major.superior-trunk.sensory_distribution: Carries the C5–C6 sensory fibres of the upper limb; upper trunk injury produces sensory loss over the lateral aspect of the upper limb.
major.superior-trunk.clinical_testing: Upper trunk (C5–C6) injury is Erb's palsy: the suprascapular, axillary and musculocutaneous nerves are predominantly affected, with loss of abduction and lateral rotation of the arm, loss of supination and loss of shoulder flexion, sensory loss on the lateral aspect of the upper limb, and the characteristic 'waiter's tip' position of the limb.
major.superior-trunk.note: Links the sided FMA 5.1.0 concept records named in geometry_record_ids; those records are geometry-absent — the FMA is an ontology and carries no mesh data (Milestone 33).

major.middle-trunk.name: Middle trunk of brachial plexus
major.middle-trunk.root_values: Formed by the anterior ramus of C7 alone.
major.middle-trunk.course: The trunk traverses the posterior triangle of the neck and divides into anterior and posterior divisions, which go on to form the cords of the plexus.
major.middle-trunk.motor_distribution: Motor fibres of C7 pass through the trunk into the lateral cord (via the anterior division) and the posterior cord (via the posterior division), and so into the terminal nerves of the upper limb; the plexus account lists no branches arising from the middle trunk itself.

major.inferior-trunk.name: Inferior trunk of brachial plexus
major.inferior-trunk.root_values: Formed by the union of the anterior rami of C8 and T1; the roots emerge between the anterior and middle scalene muscles.
major.inferior-trunk.course: The trunk traverses the posterior triangle of the neck and divides into anterior and posterior divisions; the anterior division continues as the medial cord of the plexus.
major.inferior-trunk.motor_distribution: Its fibres reach the hand via the medial cord and the ulnar and median nerves, which supply the intrinsic muscles of the hand.
major.inferior-trunk.sensory_distribution: Carries the C8–T1 sensory fibres of the upper limb; lower trunk injury produces sensory loss along the medial side of the upper limb.
major.inferior-trunk.clinical_testing: Lower trunk (C8–T1) injury is Klumpke's palsy: the ulnar and median nerves are predominantly affected, the intrinsic muscles of the hand are affected with sensory loss on the medial side of the upper limb, and the hand is left clawed.
major.inferior-trunk.note: Links the sided FMA 5.1.0 concept records named in geometry_record_ids; those records are geometry-absent — the FMA is an ontology and carries no mesh data (Milestone 33).

major.lateral-cord.name: Lateral cord of brachial plexus
major.lateral-cord.root_values: Formed by the union of the anterior divisions of the superior and middle trunks; root values C5, C6 and C7. The cords of the plexus are named by their relationship to the axillary artery.
major.lateral-cord.course: Lies lateral to the axillary artery in the axilla; gives off the lateral pectoral nerve, then divides into the musculocutaneous nerve and the lateral root of the median nerve.
major.lateral-cord.motor_distribution: Motor fibres pass into the musculocutaneous nerve (coracobrachialis, biceps brachii and brachialis) and, via the lateral root of the median nerve, into the median nerve's muscles of the forearm and hand.
major.lateral-cord.sensory_distribution: Sensory fibres pass into the musculocutaneous nerve, continuing as the lateral cutaneous nerve of the forearm (lateral forearm), and into the median nerve (lateral palm and the palmar surface of the lateral three and a half digits).

major.lateral-cord.note: Links the sided FMA 5.1.0 concept records named in geometry_record_ids; those records are geometry-absent — the FMA is an ontology and carries no mesh data (Milestone 33).

major.posterior-cord.name: Posterior cord of brachial plexus
major.posterior-cord.root_values: Formed by the union of the posterior divisions of all three trunks; root values C5–T1. The cords of the plexus are named by their relationship to the axillary artery.
major.posterior-cord.course: Lies posterior to the axillary artery in the axilla; gives off the subscapular nerves and the thoracodorsal nerve, then divides into the axillary nerve and the radial nerve.
major.posterior-cord.motor_distribution: Motor fibres pass into the axillary nerve (deltoid and teres minor) and the radial nerve (triceps brachii, brachioradialis, extensor carpi radialis longus and the posterior compartment of the forearm).
major.posterior-cord.sensory_distribution: Sensory fibres pass into the axillary nerve (skin over the inferior part of the deltoid) and the radial nerve's cutaneous branches (posterior arm, posterior forearm, lower lateral arm, and the dorsal surface of the lateral hand and digits).
verify: clinical_testing: no lesion pattern or bedside test specific to the posterior cord is described in the consulted sources; not entered - verify
major.posterior-cord.note: Links the sided FMA 5.1.0 concept records named in geometry_record_ids; those records are geometry-absent — the FMA is an ontology and carries no mesh data (Milestone 33).

major.medial-cord.name: Medial cord of brachial plexus
major.medial-cord.root_values: Formed by the anterior division of the inferior trunk; root values C8 and T1. The cords of the plexus are named by their relationship to the axillary artery.
major.medial-cord.course: Lies medial to the axillary artery in the axilla; gives off the medial pectoral nerve, the medial cutaneous nerve of the arm and the medial cutaneous nerve of the forearm, then divides into the ulnar nerve and the medial root of the median nerve.
major.medial-cord.motor_distribution: Motor fibres pass into the ulnar nerve (flexor carpi ulnaris, the medial half of flexor digitorum profundus and the intrinsic muscles of the hand) and, via the medial root of the median nerve, into the median nerve's muscles.
major.medial-cord.sensory_distribution: Gives off the medial cutaneous nerve of the arm (medial arm) and the medial cutaneous nerve of the forearm (medial forearm) directly; further sensory fibres continue into the ulnar nerve (medial palm, and the medial one and a half digits).
