structure.mons-pubis.note: The tranche's one tier-C record, and the female line's one geometry record: the dataset's entire female reproductive presence is a pad of fat the sources describe in a sentence. Recorded thin, not padded.
structure.mons-pubis.description: The pad of fat anteriorly over the pubic bone (S7): in the female it forms the surface anterior border of the perineum (S8). It is the only female-named reproductive concept in the release — filed in PART-OF under the pelvis, there being no female genital tree — and so it is the female line's only geometry (S10).

region.perineum.name: Perineum
region.perineum.note: Shared ground in every sense: one region for both sex lines, its clinical anatomy sourced whole, its geometry borrowed entire from a muscle another module owns.
region.perineum.description: An anatomical region in the pelvis, located between the thighs, representing the most inferior part of the pelvic outlet and separated from the pelvic cavity superiorly by the pelvic floor (S8). In clinical usage the word is often narrowed to the area between the external genitalia and the anus; anatomically it is the whole diamond (S8).
region.perineum.boundaries: Anatomical borders (S8): anteriorly the pubic symphysis; posteriorly the tip of the coccyx; laterally the inferior pubic rami and inferior ischial rami and the sacrotuberous ligament; the roof is the pelvic floor and the base skin and fascia. Surface borders, with the limbs abducted (S8): anteriorly the mons pubis in females, the base of the penis in males; laterally the medial surfaces of the thighs; posteriorly the superior end of the intergluteal cleft.
region.perineum.parts: A theoretical line drawn transversely between the ischial tuberosities divides the diamond into the anterior urogenital triangle and the posterior anal triangle (S8). The anal triangle — bounded by the coccyx, the sacrotuberous ligaments and the intertuberosity line — contains the anal aperture, the external anal sphincter muscle and the paired ischioanal fossae (S8). The urogenital triangle is associated with the structures of the urogenital system, the external genitalia and the urethra (S8). At the junction of the two triangles sits the perineal body, an irregular fibromuscular mass at the central point of the perineum (S8). Of these named parts, none has a concept in the release: the triangles, the perineal body and the ischioanal fossae are all zero-hit shared-line probes (S10).
region.perineum.function: The region contains the structures that support the urogenital and gastrointestinal systems, and so plays its part in micturition, defecation, sexual intercourse and childbirth (S8).
region.perineum.dataset_note: The release's perineal geometry is a single muscle's shape: the perineum and its anal part carry the same four mesh files in PART-OF, and those four files are exactly the file set of the external anal sphincter — the muscular module's record muscle.external-anal-sphincter, censused in this module as a cross-reference (S10). The sphincter is the anal triangle's one muscular content the source names (S8) and the only perineal structure the dataset draws.

organ.skin.name: Skin
organ.skin.note: The release's skin record is the shell this clinical record describes; the layers it names are the next three records, each carried over a total concept absence.
organ.skin.description: The body's protective organ: multiple layers of cells and tissues held to underlying structures by connective tissue, made of two main layers — the epidermis of closely packed epithelial cells and the dermis of dense, irregular connective tissue housing blood vessels, hair follicles, sweat glands and other structures — with the hypodermis of loose connective and fatty tissue closely associated beneath it. The skin and its accessory structures make up the integumentary system, which provides the body with overall protection (S1). In the release the skin is one concept and one whole-body mesh shell: no regional skin and no layer of it has a concept (S5).
layers: hypodermis (subcutaneous layer — closely associated, not strictly part of the skin)
organ.skin.function: Protection first: against invasion by microorganisms, chemicals and other environmental factors, against dehydration, and against UV sunlight; the skin also acts as a sensory organ, modulates body temperature and electrolyte balance, and synthesizes vitamin D — its epidermal layer produces cholecalciferol from a cholesterol derivative under UV radiation (S3).
organ.skin.cells: The epidermis is populated from the stratum basale: keratinocytes, manufactured there and pushed superficially, make and store keratin — the fibrous protein that gives skin, hair and nails their hardness and water resistance; melanocytes dispersed among the basal cells produce melanin, colouring skin and hair and shielding living epidermal cells from UV damage; Merkel cells of the basale act as touch receptors; Langerhans cells of the stratum spinosum act as macrophages (S1).
organ.skin.vascularisation: The epidermis is avascular — it has no blood vessels within it. The dermis is well vascularised, the reticular layer especially; its arterioles dilate to dissipate heat through the skin and constrict to conserve it, the skin reddening with exercise and paling in the cold (S1, S3). No consulted source names the skin's arteries individually, so no named supply is asserted.
organ.skin.innervation: The dermis carries numerous sensory, autonomic and sympathetic nerve fibres ensuring communication to and from the brain: Meissner corpuscles answering light touch and Pacinian corpuscles vibration, Merkel cells, and pain and temperature receptors scattered throughout, most concentrated at the fingertips; motor nerves supply the arrector pili muscles and the glands (S1, S3). No named cutaneous nerve is asserted — none is named by the consulted sources for the skin in general.

structure.epidermis.name: Epidermis
verify: no BP3D 4.0 concept exists for this structure (probe-verified over all six release tables by tools/integ_map.py); the record is sourced text only and links no geometry
structure.epidermis.note: Sourced text over a total absence: the release's 'subdivision of epidermis' concept (FMA70593) is a tissue class carrying the appendage line's geometry, not an epidermis — it is a grouping class of the inventory, and this record links no geometry.
structure.epidermis.description: The superficial layer of the skin: keratinized, stratified squamous epithelium, avascular, made of four or five layers of epithelial cells depending on location — four in the thin skin that covers most of the body, five in the thick skin of the palms and soles, which adds the stratum lucidum (S1). The release has no epidermis concept: its only layer-named concept is a 'subdivision of epidermis' class under which the appendages are filed (S5).
structure.epidermis.function: The barrier layer: its keratin and the water-repelling glycolipids released from the stratum spinosum upward make the skin relatively waterproof; the dry, dead stratum corneum — 15 to 30 cell layers, replaced over about four weeks — resists microbial penetration, dehydration and abrasion; and the epidermis synthesizes vitamin D under UV (S1, S3).
structure.epidermis.cells: All its cells but the basal layer's are keratinocytes, produced by mitosis in the stratum basale and pushed superficially as new cells form, flattening and dying through the granulosum until only keratin, keratohyalin and cell membranes remain at the surface (S1).
structure.epidermis.forms: Thin skin (four strata) covers most of the body; thick skin (five, with the stratum lucidum of dead, eleidin-packed keratinocytes) is found only on the palms of the hands and the soles of the feet (S1).

structure.dermis.name: Dermis
verify: no BP3D 4.0 concept exists for this structure (probe-verified over all six release tables by tools/integ_map.py); the record is sourced text only and links no geometry
structure.dermis.description: The core of the integumentary system beneath the epidermis: two layers of connective tissue composing an interconnected mesh of elastin and collagenous fibres produced by fibroblasts, containing blood and lymph vessels, nerves, hair follicles and sweat glands (S1). The release has no dermis concept (exact-name probe-verified) (S5).
structure.dermis.function: Support and supply: collagen gives the skin structure and tensile strength and binds water to keep it hydrated, elastin gives it the elasticity that enables movement; the layer houses and feeds the structures the epidermis cannot — vessels, nerves, follicles and glands — and its blood flow is the skin's radiator, dilating and constricting in thermoregulation (S1, S3).
structure.dermis.contents: The papillary layer (loose areolar tissue) projects dermal papillae into the stratum basale, strengthening the epidermal junction — their meeting with basal cells forms fingerprints — and holds fibroblasts, a few adipocytes, small vessels, phagocytes, lymphatic capillaries, nerve fibres and Meissner corpuscles; the much thicker reticular layer (dense irregular tissue) is well vascularised with a rich sensory and sympathetic nerve supply (S1).

structure.hypodermis.name: Hypodermis
verify: no BP3D 4.0 concept exists for this structure (probe-verified over all six release tables by tools/integ_map.py); the record is sourced text only and links no geometry
structure.hypodermis.note: The clinical name 'superficial fascia' for this layer is OpenStax's (S1); the release's fascial concepts are the deep investing fascia of the limbs, a different structure, rejected by this module's sweep and censused by no module (S5).
structure.hypodermis.description: The layer directly below the dermis — also called the subcutaneous layer or superficial fascia — connecting the skin to the underlying fascia of the bones and muscles. It is not strictly a part of the skin, though its border with the dermis can be difficult to distinguish (S1). The release has no hypodermis or subcutaneous concept under any name (S5).
structure.hypodermis.function: Fat storage, insulation and cushioning: its adipose tissue is an energy reserve, insulates the body against heat loss and cushions underlying structures against trauma (S1, S3).
structure.hypodermis.composition: Well-vascularised, loose areolar connective tissue and adipose tissue of fat-storing adipocytes; where the fat is deposited depends on hormones and genetic factors, and its distribution differs between males and females (S1).

structure.hair.name: Hair
verify: ta_name: not found in TA2 (FIPAT 2nd ed., version 2.07) consulted 2026-11-06 — TA2 names hairs only by region (7055 capilli, 7062 pubes, 7059 pili tragi); no generic hair term ('pilus') exists in the consulted table.
structure.hair.note: The parts list names two structures the release does not carry — the follicle and the arrector pili are probe-verified absences (S5); they are clinical anatomy from S2, not dataset concepts.
structure.hair.description: A keratinous filament growing out of the epidermis, primarily dead, keratinized cells: strands originate in an epidermal penetration of the dermis called the hair follicle, the exposed part is the shaft, the anchored part below the surface the root, ending deep in the dermis at the bulb. Accessory structures like hair embryologically originate from the epidermis and can extend down through the dermis into the hypodermis (S2). The release carries the hair class and three regional records — its appendage line's whole geometry is two mesh files (S5).
structure.hair.function: Protection, sensory input, thermoregulation and communication: hair on the head protects the skull from the sun; the sensory innervation of the hair root plexus makes hair extremely sensitive to air movement and disturbance; and each root's arrector pili muscle, contracting on sympathetic signals, raises the shaft to trap an insulating layer of air — visible in humans as goose bumps (S2).
structure.hair.growth_cycle: Growth in three phases: anagen, cells dividing rapidly at the root, lasting typically 2 to 7 years; catagen, 2 to 3 weeks of transition; telogen, 2 to 4 months of rest, after which a new hair pushes the old out. Hair grows about 0.3 mm per day in anagen, and on average 50 hairs are lost and replaced per day (S2).
structure.hair.colour: Hair takes its colour from melanin produced by melanocytes in the hair papilla; the type of melanin is genetically determined, and as production decreases with age the hair greys and whitens (S2).

structure.hair-of-head.name: Hair of head
structure.hair-of-head.description: The hair of the scalp — in the release a regional record of the hair class with its own mesh file (FJ2813), the head half of the hair geometry's two-file partition (S5). As hair, it is the keratinous filament of S2, growing from follicles of the scalp's epidermis.
structure.hair-of-head.function: Hair on the head protects the skull from the sun (S2).

structure.hair-of-trunk.name: Hair of trunk
verify: function: not asserted — no consulted source treats trunk hair separately from hair in general; the general functions are carried on structure.hair and are not repeated here as if they were region-specific
ta_name: not found in TA2 (FIPAT 2nd ed., version 2.07) consulted 2026-11-06 — no TA2 term for hair of the trunk in the consulted table; TA2's regional hair terms cover head, pubis and tragus only.
structure.hair-of-trunk.note: Recorded thin by design (the mons pubis precedent, Milestone 14): the dataset gives the region a record and a mesh; the consulted literature gives it no separate account.
structure.hair-of-trunk.description: The hair of the trunk — in the release a regional record of the hair class, sharing its single mesh file (FJ2815) with its child, the pubic hair (S5). As hair, it is the keratinous filament of S2.

structure.pubic-hair.name: Pubic hair
verify: function: not asserted — no consulted source treats pubic hair separately from hair in general; the general functions are carried on structure.hair
structure.pubic-hair.note: The one clinical record of this tranche whose dataset concept sits in two modules' filings; the concept is owned by this module's inventory and cross-filed under the reproductive module's mons pubis (S5).
structure.pubic-hair.description: The hair of the pubic region — in the release filed two ways: IS-A under hair of trunk in this module's line, and PART-OF under the mons pubis, the reproductive module's only female record; it shares the trunk hair's mesh file (FJ2815) in both tables (S5). As hair, it is the keratinous filament of S2.

structure.eyebrow.name: Eyebrow
structure.eyebrow.description: The hair of the brow — in the release a single concept under 'set of facial hairs', resolving with both of its set classes to one mesh file (FJ2812); the only named facial hair the release carries, there being no eyelash concept in it (S5).
structure.eyebrow.function: Hair of the eyebrows prevents sweat and other particles from dripping into and bothering the eyes (S2).

structure.nail.name: Nail
verify: no BP3D 4.0 concept exists for this structure (probe-verified over all six release tables by tools/integ_map.py); the record is sourced text only and links no geometry
structure.nail.description: An accessory structure formed on a specialized structure of the epidermis at the tips of the fingers and toes: the nail body, composed of densely packed dead keratinocytes, is formed on the nail bed and grows continuously from a matrix of proliferating cells of the stratum basale at the nail root (S2). The release has no nail concept in any form — 'nail' and 'unguis' are zero-hit in all six tables (S5).
structure.nail.function: The nail body protects the tips of the fingers and toes — the farthest extremities, under the maximum mechanical stress — and forms a back-support for picking up small objects with the fingers (S2).

gland.sebaceous-glands.name: Sebaceous glands
verify: no BP3D 4.0 concept exists for this structure (probe-verified over all six release tables by tools/integ_map.py); the record is sourced text only and links no geometry
gland.sebaceous-glands.description: Oil glands found all over the body, most of them associated with hair follicles, generating and excreting sebum onto the skin surface (S2). The release has no sebaceous concept — 'sebaceous' is zero-hit in all six tables (S5).
gland.sebaceous-glands.secretion: Sebum, a mixture of lipids, excreted onto the skin surface and into the follicle (S2).
gland.sebaceous-glands.function: To lubricate and waterproof the skin and hair: sebum keeps the dry, dead keratinized layer of the stratum corneum pliable, its fatty acids are antibacterial, and it prevents water loss from the skin in low-humidity environments (S2).
gland.sebaceous-glands.activation: Sebum secretion is stimulated by hormones, many of which do not become active until puberty, so the glands are relatively inactive during childhood (S2). The areola's sebaceous glands enlarge during pregnancy, secreting an oily lubricant for the nipple (S4).

gland.sweat-glands.name: Sweat glands
verify: no BP3D 4.0 concept exists for this structure (probe-verified over all six release tables by tools/integ_map.py); the record is sourced text only and links no geometry
gland.sweat-glands.note: The mammary gland record that follows is this gland family's other member by kind: the consulted source defines the mammary glands as modified sweat glands (S4).
gland.sweat-glands.description: Sudoriferous glands that develop from epidermal projections into the dermis, classified as merocrine glands — their secretions are excreted by exocytosis through a duct without affecting the gland's cells. There are two types, eccrine and apocrine, each secreting a slightly different product (S2). The release has no sweat-gland concept — 'sweat' and 'sudoriferous' are zero-hit in all six tables (S5).
types: eccrine sweat gland — a coiled gland lying deep in the dermis, its duct rising to a pore on the surface; found all over the skin but especially abundant on the palms, soles and forehead; produces a hypotonic sweat of mostly water with some salt, antibodies, traces of metabolic waste and the antimicrobial peptide dermcidin

apocrine sweat gland — larger and deeper, usually associated with hair follicles in densely hairy areas such as the armpits and genital regions, its duct normally emptying into the follicle; its sweat adds organic compounds that thicken it and subject it to bacterial decomposition and smell; release is under both nervous and hormonal control
gland.sweat-glands.function: Thermoregulation: when the body becomes warm the glands produce sweat to cool it — a primary component of temperature homeostasis, under sympathetic control, from about 500 mL a day of insensible perspiration to 0.7-1.5 litres per hour in an active person; the sweat's dermcidin also deters microbes from over-colonizing the skin surface (S2, S3).

organ.mammary-gland.name: Mammary gland and breast
verify: no BP3D 4.0 concept exists for this structure (probe-verified over all six release tables by tools/integ_map.py); the record is sourced text only and links no geometry

ta_name: ambiguous in TA2 (FIPAT 2nd ed., version 2.07) consulted 2026-11-06 — compound record ('mammary gland and breast'): TA2 terms 7097 mamma (breast) and 7099 glandula mammaria (mammary gland) each denote part of what this single record covers; neither denotes the whole.
organ.mammary-gland.note: The tranche's closing record and the module's argument, as the ovary was Milestone 14's: complete sourced clinical anatomy for a structure the dataset does not contain, with the absence recorded on the record and its ownership decided in the open, on a stated basis.
organ.mammary-gland.description: The breasts are paired structures on the anterior thoracic wall in the pectoral region, present in both males and females and more prominent in females following puberty; in females they contain the mammary glands, the key structures involved in lactation. The mammary glands are modified sweat glands: a series of ducts and secretory lobules (15-20) surrounded by a connective tissue stroma (S4). The release carries no mammary, breast, nipple or areola concept under any name — the gland exists in this module as this record alone (S5).
organ.mammary-gland.function: Lactation: the gland produces and secretes milk, each lobule's alveoli draining by a single lactiferous duct, the ducts converging at the nipple like spokes of a wheel. Production and secretion are regulated by the hormones prolactin and oxytocin from the pituitary gland — not by the breast's own nerves (S4).
organ.mammary-gland.relations: The breast extends horizontally from the lateral border of the sternum to the mid-axillary line and vertically between the 2nd and 6th costal cartilages, lying superficially to the pectoralis major and serratus anterior; its base lies on the pectoral fascia, with the loose connective tissue of the retromammary space between, and the suspensory ligaments attach it to the dermis and the pectoral fascia and separate its lobules (S4).
organ.mammary-gland.arterial_supply: The medial aspect is supplied by the internal thoracic artery, a branch of the subclavian; the lateral part by four vessels — the lateral thoracic and thoracoacromial branches of the axillary artery, the lateral mammary branches of the posterior intercostal arteries in the 2nd, 3rd and 4th spaces, and the mammary branch of the anterior intercostal artery (S4). The vessels are named here as the source names them; no cardiovascular record ids are asserted for them.
organ.mammary-gland.venous_drainage: The veins correspond with the arteries, draining into the axillary and internal thoracic veins (S4).
organ.mammary-gland.lymphatic_drainage: Of great clinical importance for the metastasis of breast cancer: three node groups receive the breast's lymph — the axillary nodes (75%), the parasternal nodes (20%) and the posterior intercostal nodes (5%). The skin of the breast drains to the axillary, inferior deep cervical and infraclavicular nodes, and the nipple and areola to the subareolar lymphatic plexus (S4).
organ.mammary-gland.innervation: The anterior and lateral cutaneous branches of the 4th to 6th intercostal nerves, carrying sensory and autonomic fibres — the autonomic fibres regulating smooth muscle and blood vessel tone. These nerves do not control the production and secretion of milk (S4).
organ.mammary-gland.ownership: Ownership adjudication, recorded as this module's decision: the dataset cannot decide the question — the release files the mammary gland under neither the integumentary nor the reproductive system, having no concept for it under any name (S5) — so the record is placed by classification. It is owned HERE, in the integumentary module, because the consulted clinical source defines the mammary glands as modified sweat glands (S4): cutaneous glands by kind, of a piece with this module's sebaceous and sweat gland records, and developmentally an appendage of the skin. The counter-consideration is recorded, not suppressed: the same source introduces the glands as 'an accessory gland of the female reproductive system', and lactation is reproductive function. The reproductive module (Milestone 14) completed its census of the release without claiming any mammary name, so no module boundary is crossed by placing the record here; the placement is a stated convention of this project, not a fact of the dataset, and the reproductive module's records cross-reference it by this id.
